subject: Request: temporary fallback carveout & region-only routing for FinEdge prod
messages:
From: Sarah Brown <sarah.brown@finedge.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinEdge Compliance Team <compliance@finedge.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0500
Subject: Production requirement: no-fallback + eu-west-1 routing for model 'fin-qa-1'

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Two compliance items popped up during our internal review that block go-live unless addressed by Redwood:

1) We cannot allow any automatic fallback to alternative models for prod traffic that handles customer PII. The model must be deterministic and auditable (they've requested forced selection of 'fin-qa-1' for the eu-prod route).
2) Traffic must be pinned to eu-west-1 (region lock) — FinEdge regulatory rules require processing within the EEA.

We understand this is an operational deviation from default Redwood routing. We're requesting a 90-day carveout while our auditors complete the attestation. Ideally this is a config toggle on your side; if not, we'll need a short-term SOW to fund engineering changes.

Attached: product requirements summary and a short SOW draft. Happy to hop on a call today if that helps.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Brown
Head of Platform Security, FinEdge Capital
Attachments: finedge_prod_requirements.pdf (pdf, 42KB), finedge_sow_2026_v2.docx (docx, 28KB)
From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0500
Subject: Fwd: Production requirement: no-fallback + eu-west-1 routing for model 'fin-qa-1'

Folks — forwarding FinEdge's ask. Short summary: they need (A) no-fallback enforced to a single model for prod (fin-qa-1) and (B) strict region pinning to eu-west-1 for 90 days while auditors finish up. They asked whether this can be a config toggle vs engineering change + SOW.

Can product/infra weigh in on feasibility, risk, and options (config toggle, runtime policy, per-customer routing rule, or contract-limited exception)? They flagged this as a go/no-go for their launch next week.

Thanks,
Grace
--
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production requirement: no-fallback + eu-west-1 routing for model 'fin-qa-1'

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 08:12 AM Sarah Brown <sarah.brown@finedge.com> wrote:
> Hi Grace,
> 
> Thanks again for the demo last week. Two compliance items popped up ...

TL;DR: Both asks are doable but have operational and risk tradeoffs. Options and impact below.

Option A — Temporary runtime policy (recommended 90-day):
- Implement a per-account routing policy that pins requests to eu-west-1 and forces model selection to fin-qa-1.
- Enforce no-fallback by disabling automatic model variant fallback for that account.
- Risks: reduces our ability to fail over on infra incidents; increases latency tail if fin-qa-1 becomes slow or queued.
- Effort: ~2 engineer-days (policy + console toggle + automated test) + 1 infra ops day to validate rollout.

Option B — Code change to hard-enforce routing in serving layer (safer for availability):
- Make a serving-runtime hard check to refuse requests that would otherwise fallback.
- Effort: ~1 week dev + QA; higher testing burden, but cleaner semantics.

Option C — Contract SOW for dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 with pinned model (most reliable):
- Dedicated pool + reserved slots for FinEdge; avoids shared queue interference.
- Commercial negotiation required; sales & finance to align.

Questions for Security/Trust (Rishi):
- Acceptable risk window if we disable fallback? (e.g., SLAs, incident escalation path)
- Any additional audit hooks they need (logs, KV-cache dumps, model hashes)?

Grace: I can prep a one-page technical note for the customer that lays out options and a recommended path. If they are OK funding a short SOW, option C is the cleanest. If they need a fast turn, we can do Option A with tight monitoring and automated rollback.

— Karthik
Product Manager, Routing & Serving
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production requirement: no-fallback + eu-west-1 routing for model 'fin-qa-1' — provisional approval + conditions

Thanks for the clear options. I'm provisionally OK with Option A (runtime policy toggle) for a time-limited carveout, provided the following controls are in place before we flip anything: 

1) Incident escalation: FinEdge must accept a temporary SLA deviation for availability and agree to an on-call escalation path that includes FinEdge ops + Redwood infra.
2) Audit hooks: We will provide model hash attribution, per-request route logs, and a KV-cache snapshot export for the carveout window.

Required steps (owners & ETA):
- Karthik: policy toggle + console UI + unit tests — ETA 48 hours.
- Infra (Laura): staging validation in eu-west-1 & load test — ETA 24 hours after Karthik's change.
- Grace: confirm FinEdge signs the carveout SOW (<=90 days) and agrees to the SLA deviation and escalation contacts — ETA EOD tomorrow.

Operational notes:
- We'll implement an automatic rollback policy: if fin-qa-1 latency 95th percentile > 800ms for 10 min, toggle will auto-disable and we will notify FinEdge immediately.
- We'll enable extra monitoring and a dedicated PagerDuty rotation for the first 72 hours.

Once Grace confirms the SOW and contacts, we'll schedule the change window and notify FinEdge of the risk and rollback plan.

Rishi
Head of Reliability & Security
Redwood Inference
